name: Butter Crackers
description: Historical recipe from Common Sense in the Household (1871). Source method; not modernized or kitchen-tested.

ingredients.name: ½ teaspoonful soda, dissolved in hot water
ingredients.originalText: ½ teaspoonful soda, dissolved in hot water

instructions.text: Rub the butter into the flour, or cut it up with a knife or chopper, as you do in pastry
Add the salt, milk, and soda, mixing well
Beat with a rolling-pin half an hour, turning and shifting the mass often
Roll into an even sheet, a quarter of an inch thick, or less
Bake hard in a moderate oven
Hang them up in a muslin bag in the kitchen for two days to dry

source.author: Marion Harland
source.originalInstructions:
1. Rub the butter into the flour, or cut it up with a knife or chopper, as you do in pastry
2. Add the salt, milk, and soda, mixing well
3. Work into a ball
4. Lay upon a floured board
5. Beat with a rolling-pin half an hour, turning and shifting the mass often
6. Roll into an even sheet, a quarter of an inch thick, or less
7. Prick deeply with a fork
8. Bake hard in a moderate oven
9. Hang them up in a muslin bag in the kitchen for two days to dry
